decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures proportional transfer and preservation of the second V, but leaves the prior sharp terminal treatment stale after the client requests a softer, non-calligraphic terminal.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Kenji,

Although the three reference lines are useful for evaluating the second V and the accent, this iteration has completely lost the Hero V—the foundation of the entire system.

Please respect both our time by ensuring that the Hero V, along with the established proportions of the second V and accent, continues to follow the rules we have already agreed upon.

The next round should address only the following:

Restore the Hero V.
Finalize its terminal language so it is softer, but not calligraphic.
After those elements are correct, transfer them to the É accent and then apply them proportionally to the second V.

Whenever the foundation disappears, the project moves 3 steps backward. Until the Hero V is restored and the VvÉ hierarchy is reestablished, every other consideration is secondary.

value_updates.terminal_derivation: Apply the Hero V's finalized soft but non-calligraphic architectural terminal proportionally to the second V while preserving its subordinate role.
value_updates.terminal_treatment: soft but non-calligraphic architectural terminal applied proportionally from the finalized Hero V
value_updates.right_endpoint_adjustment_method: Retain the selected endpoint-height calibration calculated from the second V's own height and preserve its established proportions and non-terminal geometry while applying the finalized terminal treatment proportionally.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY records exact transfer from the restored Hero V but fails to replace the accent's stale sharp terminal treatment with the newly requested soft, non-calligraphic treatment.
